lines.speaker: survivor_ives
lines.text: Mind the third bridge. It's rope over rope now, has been since spring, when we lost a man off it. We still call it the good one.

lines.speaker: survivor_ives
lines.text: Forty-one of us on these roofs. My grandmother used to say nine million lived down there, and I told her to stop lying to children, and then I got old enough to find the census.

lines.speaker: survivor_ives
lines.text: There's a thing in the stairwells. Comes up with the tide. Looks like someone you knew, and sounds like them, and it is not them. Don't answer it. That's not superstition, that's a rule with names attached.

lines.speaker: survivor_ives
lines.text: You went down there, then. Nobody's done that in my lifetime and come back up talking, and I'd like it noted that I'm not asking what you saw.

lines.speaker: survivor_ives
lines.text: Water's lower this year. Two steps lower on the east stair. Nobody can tell me why and I've stopped asking the kind of question that hasn't got an answer, but I've noticed, and I've told people to notice.

lines.speaker: survivor_ives
lines.text: Heard your century's got walls and rations and a machine doing the counting. Ours has got weather and forty-one people who know each other's names. I'll keep the weather.
